script.title: Jay Gould tried to corner America's gold. Then Grant moved 🤯
script.hook_text: Gould tries to corner America's gold
sentences: Jay Gould tried to corner America's gold through the President's brother-in-law.
It was 1869, and Corbin could get Gould close to President Grant.
Gould bribed the assistant treasurer with $10,000, more than his yearly salary.
He opened a $500,000 gold account for Grant's secretary, who refused in writing.
The Treasury paused its extra gold sales, while Gould and Jim Fisk kept buying.
On September 24 he released $4 million in government gold.
The price collapsed, Wall Street panicked, and that day became Black Friday.
Gould and Fisk hired the best defense available and escaped prosecution.
script.description:
Before Black Friday meant shopping, it meant a gold panic.
September 24, 1869.
claims_en: Jay Gould tried to corner the gold market with the help of Abel Corbin, President Grant's brother-in-law
Gould used Corbin's relationship to get close to President Ulysses S. Grant
Gould bribed assistant treasurer Daniel Butterfield with a $10,000 check, more than his annual salary of $8,000
Gould opened a $500,000 gold account in the name of Grant's secretary Horace Porter, who refused it in writing
Treasury Secretary Boutwell suspended non-routine Treasury gold sales for the rest of the month
Gould and Fisk continued buying gold
Grant learned about the nature of the scheme
On September 24 Grant ordered the release of $4 million in government gold
The price of gold dropped and a panic on Wall Street ensued, known as Black Friday
Gould and Fisk hired the best defense available and escaped prosecution
scenes: Extreme close-up of a thin, bearded 1860s financier's face, dark eyes narrowed in calculation, lit by gaslight in a smoky office
An 1869 drawing room where a smooth-talking middle-aged man introduces the bearded financier to a stern bearded president in a dark frock coat, gaslight, medium shot
The financier sliding a bank check across a desk to a nervous former general in civilian clothes, close framing on hands and faces, 1860s office
A young military-looking secretary at a desk writing a firm letter of refusal, a gold certificate set aside, lamplight
A crowded 1869 Gold Room with traders shouting and waving their hands, the financier and a flamboyant partner in a striped vest watching from the side, smug
The stern bearded president alone at his desk reading a report, his face hardening, window light, close-up
A gold price board in the 1869 Gold Room as clerks frantically chalk falling numbers, close framing
Chaos on an 1869 Wall Street, men in top hats running and shouting in the street, papers flying, overcast sky, wide shot
The financier and his flamboyant partner walking calmly down courthouse steps with lawyers in frock coats, cool daylight
